original_question: For a hyperkahler manifold X, determine which integral quadratic forms can occur as the Beauville-Bogomolov form q on H^2(X, Z), whether q must always be even, and which values can occur for the Fujiki constant f_X defined by the relation integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r in dimension 2r.
target_in_paper: Section 1.4 ("Cohomology"), Question 3, using the notation introduced in Section 1.3 ("The period map").
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's actual target: Beauville's Question 3 asks, for a hyperkähler manifold X, whether the Beauville-Bogomolov quadratic form q on H^2(X,Z) is always even, what forms q can occur, and what values the Fujiki constant/index f_X can take through the Fujiki relation in complex dimension 2r.
missing_details: X should be specified as a compact hyperkähler manifold (irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold) over C, matching the paper's standing setup.
The paper defines q as the canonical primitive quadratic form q: H^2(X,Z) -> Z; this primitiveness is part of the data and should be stated.
The paper records that q has signature (3, b_2(X) - 3), so the question is not about arbitrary integral quadratic forms but about primitive forms of that signature arising from hyperkähler manifolds.
The Fujiki relation is stated for every alpha in H^2(X,Z), not just for some class alpha.
The dimension assumption should be tied explicitly to the relation: if dim(X) = 2r, then integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r.
The nearby context distinguishes the name 'Fujiki constant' from the wording in Question 3, which calls the same invariant the 'Fujiki index' f_X.
The surrounding paragraph notes that all known examples discussed there have even Beauville-Bogomolov form; that motivation is part of why the evenness question is asked.
To stay closest to the paper, the question should ask for the possible q and possible f_X attached to the same manifold X, rather than treating them as unrelated classification problems.
refined_question: Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold of complex dimension 2r, and let q: H^2(X,Z) -> Z be its canonical primitive Beauville-Bogomolov quadratic form, characterized by the Fujiki relation integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r for every alpha in H^2(X,Z), where f_X is the Fujiki constant/index. Must q always be even? More generally, which primitive integral quadratic forms q (necessarily of signature (3, b_2(X) - 3)) can occur on H^2(X,Z), and which values can occur for f_X?
justification: This is exactly the open problem stated as Question 3 in Section 1.4. Section 1.3 supplies the definitions that your draft needs in order to be stand-alone: q is the canonical primitive quadratic form on H^2(X,Z), it has signature (3, b_2 - 3), and f_X is defined by the Fujiki relation for every alpha in H^2(X,Z). Proposition 1 in Section 1.4 explains why q is central to the cohomology of X, and the paragraph immediately preceding Question 3 notes that the known examples then available all had even lattices, including O'Grady's examples. So your draft is already aimed at the right problem; the refinement mainly restores the paper's exact scope and notation without broadening it.
